tasks.title: Implement nested stint drain parent-chain handling
tasks.description:
Context: Follow-up from add-stints review, now planned as prerequisite section 0 of openspec/changes/add-stints-gating. Current drain identifies the completed stint by file but only searches root for the matching ref, so a nested graph like root -> auth -> search cannot mark auth's search ref done or archive search when search drains. This must be fixed before gating relies on final-lap drain/archive behavior under hold. Implements add-stints-gating tasks 0.1-0.4.

Outcome: Active resolution or drain preparation returns the physical parent chain for every descended stint ref: parent path, parent file, ref index/pointer, child path, child name, and canonical scope. Completing the final lap in a nested stint updates the immediate parent ref, archives the child file, and cascades upward while parent stints have no todo laps. Root-level drain behavior remains unchanged. Cross-stint done undo restores archived nested stint files and reopens the immediate parent ref plus any ancestor refs/files needed to make the reopened lap reachable.

Files & scope: internal/cmd/resolution.go and internal/cmd/done.go primarily; store archive helpers only if a small helper is needed. Do not implement hold/release or exit-code gating in this lap.

Design: Preserve the add-stints invariants. Cycle detection stays keyed on physical child identity, not slash scope. Drain remains content-based and position-independent. Partial-failure ordering applies at each cascade level: preflight archive/save targets before mutation; if archive rename succeeds but saving the parent/root ref fails, restore the archived file back to active before returning. Never leave a done parent ref over a present active child file, or a todo parent ref pointing at a missing active child file when the archived file exists.

Acceptance: just build and just test green. Manual reasoning confirms root-level drain and undo behavior are not regressed.

tasks.title: Write nested stint drain and undo regression tests
tasks.description:

Outcome: Focused tests cover nested drain and undo behavior: completing the final lap in root -> auth -> search marks the search ref inside auth done and archives search; draining search cascades to archive auth when auth has no remaining todo laps; archive collision or simulated save failure at a nested level leaves no dangling parent ref; done undo for an archived nested lap restores child file, ancestor refs/files, and the lap.

Files & scope: internal/cmd/cmd_test.go and/or focused helper tests near the drain code. No production code changes unless a tiny testability fix is required.

Design: Tests must inspect both files and refs, not only command output. The partial-failure regression must assert both forbidden states are absent: no done parent ref over a present active child file, and no todo parent ref pointing at a missing active child file when the archived child exists. The undo test must confirm the reopened lap is reachable through active resolution after restore.

Acceptance: just test green. just lint clean if golangci-lint is available.

tasks.title: Implement exitState and typed held-aware resolver
tasks.description:
Context: This is the LOAD-BEARING, high-risk lap of the whole change. Read design.md Implementation Contracts in full before coding. Today `exit()` (internal/cmd/root.go:39-51) ALWAYS writes a `laps:` stderr line (or an `{error,exitCode}` JSON object to STDERR), and the ONLY way a nonzero OS code is produced is `panic(*exitError)` -> recover -> `os.Exit` (root.go:50, 57-64); the deferred after-hook `runAfterHooksDeferred` (internal/cmd/hooks.go:32-51, registered at get.go:46 / claim.go:46) reads `*exitCode` ONLY during that panic unwind. So a naive `os.Exit(11)` or `return`-with-error SKIPS the after-hook and violates 'hook sees the code'.

Outcome: (a) a dedicated `exitState(code int)` helper; (b) a single TYPED queue-state (`lap | held | empty | complete`) returned by the flow-start resolver; (c) held detection — at each context head, a held `kind:"stint"` ref returns `held` and SHALL NOT descend into the child file. Do NOT wire exit codes into the get/claim nil-site yet (that is the next impl lap); do NOT touch status yet.

Files & scope: internal/cmd/root.go for exitState; the add-stints flow-start resolver (locate it in the merged tree) for the typed queue-state return and held-no-descent. Keep the resolver signature change additive so get/claim and the status probe can both consume one resolution pass.

Design (load-bearing — implement exactly): `exitState(code)` (1) sets the captured `exitCode = code`, (2) in JSON mode prints the small queue-state object to STDOUT via `printJSON` (note: `exit()` puts JSON on STDERR — this stdout-vs-stderr split IS the contract), (3) panics `*exitError{code}` with NO stderr error line. Held cases additionally warn on STDERR. Routing 10/11/12 through the existing panic/recover path is precisely what keeps `runAfterHooksDeferred` firing — do not bypass it. The resolver returns ONE typed outcome shared by get/claim and the later status gate probe (one resolution pass, not two); a held kind:"stint" ref at a context head returns held and does not descend.

Acceptance: `just build` + `just test` + `just lint` green. Include focused regression tests now (not deferred): the after-hook observes exit code 11 (the critical assertion proving the mechanism), and held-no-descent returns the held state without selecting a lap. The broader exit-code matrix is a later lap; do not tick tasks.md boxes.

tasks.title: Wire get/claim exit codes and explicit-id held behavior
tasks.description:
Context: exitState + the typed resolver exist (prior lap, verified). Now wire the exit codes at the existing post-defer `task == nil` site. That site (get.go:49-52 / claim.go:49-55) is ALREADY after the after-hook defer (get.go:46 / claim.go:46), so NO reordering is needed — the hook already observes the code. Read design.md Implementation Contracts (Empty/complete split, Existing failures keep existing codes) and Resolved Product Calls (empty-vs-complete DECIDED) before coding.

Outcome: head/flow `get`/`claim` exit `0` (lap), `10` (held), `11` (empty), `12` (complete). The empty-vs-complete DECIDED mapping: `12` = everything resolvable from the root head is done AND nothing enqueueable remains; `11` = root resolves to zero todo because nothing was enqueued (incl. only-unqueued stint files / empty active stint file). Explicit `get <id>` into a held stint returns the lap AND warns on stderr; explicit `claim <id>` into a held stint exits `10`, leaves the claim unchanged, and warns.

Files & scope: get.go and claim.go — replace the single `exit(3,"no head task")` at the post-defer nil-site with `exitState(11)` vs `exitState(12)` per the typed resolver's outcome, and add the explicit-id-held behavior (warn for get; exit 10 + no mutation for claim). Leave `checkDefault`'s `exit(2)`-on-corrupt and explicit-id-not-found `exit(3)` unchanged; `checkDefault`'s `ErrEmptyState->exit(3)` branch is DEAD (nothing returns ErrEmptyState) — leave it.

Design: 11/12 apply ONLY to head/flow ops NOT targeting an explicit id; 10 ALSO applies to explicit `claim <id>` into a held stint. Explicit-id-not-found stays exit 3; store/io stays 2; hook stays 4. Drive the 11-vs-12 and held-vs-lap decisions from the single typed resolver outcome — do not re-derive state ad-hoc in each command.

Acceptance: `just build` + `just lint` green. Smoke-check each of 0/10/11/12 by hand against fixture files (the full matrix is the next lap). Do not tick tasks.md boxes.

tasks.title: Make done work under hold with drain still winning
tasks.description:
Context: gating (§2) is verified. `done` for the already-claimed lap must succeed while a stint is held, and final-lap completion must still drain/archive so a held drained stint does not get stuck as the next gate. Read design.md 'Final-lap drain still wins' and the spec 'Hold blocks starting, not finishing'.

Outcome: `done` for the claimed lap succeeds while its stint (or the head stint) is held (3.1). Final-lap completion under hold runs the normal add-stints drain/archive behavior; the next flow state after a final-lap `done` under hold is next-lap / empty / complete — NOT held-by-the-drained-stint (3.2). Tests for 3.3.

Files & scope: done.go and the drain/archive path added by add-stints. The gating resolver from §2 must let a completed-and-drained stint fall out of the head even if its metadata is still held.

Design: hold blocks STARTING (get/claim), never FINISHING (done). The subtlety is the final-lap case: draining/archiving a held stint on its last lap MUST advance the head past it, otherwise the held drained stint stays the next gate forever. Confirm the resolver's held check only fires for stints that still have a head ref pointing into them — a drained/archived stint no longer does.

Acceptance: `just test` + `just lint` green. Tests (3.3): non-final claimed lap completes under hold and next `get`/`claim` exits 10; final claimed lap completes under hold and next flow state is next-lap/empty/complete rather than held. Do not tick tasks.md boxes.

tasks.title: Add held state to status with active-claim precedence
tasks.description:
Context: the typed resolver from §2 is shared by the status gate probe — status derives its state from ONE resolution pass, not a second ad-hoc detection. Read the spec 'Held state in status' and design.md 'Status precedence'. This EXTENDS the status taxonomy added by add-event-log-and-status; the merged set of status.state values is active/ready/empty/complete/held.

Outcome: a valid active claim keeps `status.state=active` with held gate metadata included SEPARATELY when the next head is held (4.1). When there is no valid active claim and the next flow-start would gate, status reports primary `held` state, the held stint, and the gate message; exits 0 for valid snapshots (4.2). `--json-output` reflects held with the resolved clean-state shape (4.3). Tests for 4.4.

Files & scope: the status command (internal/cmd, from add-event-log-and-status) and the resolver's typed queue-state. Reuse the same resolver outcome as get/claim.

Design: status precedence — a valid active claim ALWAYS wins (state=active; held gate metadata is a separate field). `held` is primary only when no valid active claim exists AND the next flow-start operation would gate. The empty-vs-complete DECIDED mapping (12 = all resolvable done + nothing enqueueable; 11 = nothing enqueued) also governs status empty/complete. Consumers MUST NOT treat the original four states as a closed list — surface held as a first-class state in both text and JSON. Status stays exit 0 for valid snapshots.

Acceptance: `just test` + `just lint` green. Tests (4.4): held state in text and JSON; active-claim precedence over the held gate (state=active + separate gate metadata). Do not tick tasks.md boxes.
